records.summary: President Salva Kiir Mayardit removed Dier Tong Ngor as Governor of the Bank of South Sudan by republican decree with effect from 3 January 2022, the decree citing article 182/7 of the Transitional Constitution as its authority and read out on the state broadcaster. Radio Tamazuj states that the President removed him 'without giving reasons', so no cause is asserted here beyond the act of removal itself; the decree's effective date of 3 January 2022 is given on the page. This is a separate removal from the one the map already holds for South Sudan (the June 2025 firing of a later governor, index 106).
records.source_title: President Kiir removes Central Bank Governor Dier Tong — Radio Tamazuj, 4 January 2022

records.kind: judicial raid on the central bank
records.summary: Mount Lebanon prosecuting judge Ghada Aoun authorised a judicial raid on the Banque du Liban headquarters in Beirut, entering the building in an attempt to execute an arrest of Governor Riad Salameh, whom she had charged with falsifying the bank's budget to hide losses; she said permission to arrest him had been given and then revoked by another judicial authority, and she did not enter his office. Bank employees then began a three-day strike in protest at what they called the judge's tactics. The Al Jazeera report is dated 20 July 2022 and places the raid on 'Tuesday' with the strike beginning 'Wednesday'; it prints no calendar date for the raid, so this record is dated to the month only rather than printing a day the page does not give. This is a distinct episode from the September 2024 arrest of Salameh already on the map (index 30).
records.source_title: Lebanon Central Bank workers strike after judge raids HQ — Al Jazeera, 20 July 2022

records.kind: auditor general finding against the bank
records.summary: In his Annual General Report on the Financial Statements of Public Authorities and Other Bodies for the financial year 2007/2008, submitted to President Jakaya Mrisho Kikwete on 26 March 2009 under Article 143 of the Constitution, Controller and Auditor General Ludovick S. L. Utouh found against the Bank of Tanzania over insurance for its Head Office project. Section 4.1.4, headed 'Irregular payments in respect of Insurance Premiums for BOT HQ Building Shs. 7.3 Billion', records that the Bank lacks relevant, sufficient and appropriate supporting documents such as insurance policies, endorsements or policy covers, that premiums charged and paid to the broker 'appear excessive', and that in the CAG's opinion premiums may have been paid for no insurance policies at all; he directed that management 'should institute a competent independent investigation on the transactions and take appropriate action'. The detailed finding gives total insurance premiums of US$ 6,302,823.42 paid by the Bank to its insurance broker between 20 February 2003 and 24 July 2007, against insurance policies held by the Bank supporting only US$ 2,478,388 of premiums paid — those are the report's own two labels, premiums paid and premiums supported by policies. The report's summary of recommendations repeats that BOT management should investigate the circumstances of the Tshs 7.3 billion payment 'with a view of fixing responsibilities to parties involved'. This is a state oversight organ correcting the central bank and is a separate matter from the External Payment Arrears affair behind the January 2008 dismissal of Governor Daudi Ballali already on the map (index 150); the same report separately notes the Bank's plan to engage a consultant to review the status of EPA liabilities.
records.source_title: Annual General Report of the Controller and Auditor General on the Financial Statements of Public Authorities and Other Bodies for the financial year 2007/2008, National Audit Office of Tanzania, 26 March 2009 (sections 4.1.4 and the Insurance for Construction of Head Office building at BoT finding)

records.summary: The Kathmandu Post reports that the parliamentary Finance Committee has proposed amendments to the Nepal Rastra Bank Act that would cut the governor's, deputy governors' and three independent directors' tenure from five years to three, with the Cabinet able to extend them by two more, and would keep the government's power to issue directives to the central bank, a power dating from a 2016 amendment to section 106(c) of the 2002 Act. The paper reports that Nepal Rastra Bank officials are concerned the amendments could weaken the bank's independence, consider the tenure and directive provisions the most sensitive, and had proposed removing the directive power; these are the newspaper's characterisations of the officials' position, not a statement by the bank. Committee chair Krishna Hari Budhathoki is quoted defending the change: 'If someone is not performing well, they should not simply remain in office.' Former governors and finance ministers named in the report (Yubaraj Khatiwada, Barshaman Pun, Bijaya Nath Bhattarai and Chiranjibi Nepal) warn of instability and political interference. The date is the article's publication date, 13 September 2026; the report gives no tabling or committee date. This is distinct from the April 2022 suspension of Governor Maha Prasad Adhikari already on the map (index 151).
records.source_title: Lawmakers want a shorter governor term, experts fear instability in central bank — The Kathmandu Post, 13 September 2026

records.kind: parliamentary inquiry recommends the bank president's dismissal
records.summary: The Asamblea Legislativa's Comisión para el Control del Ingreso y Gasto Públicos approved, by six votes to three, a report recommending that President Rodrigo Chaves urgently dismiss Róger Madrigal as head of the Banco Central de Costa Rica, the report's phrase being 'la urgente destitución del jerarca del Banco Central de Costa Rica'. The commission's stated grounds are that the central bank breached data-protection rules in requesting individualised personal data on bank clients from the supervisor SUGEF and four commercial banks, Madrigal's 'falta de cumplimiento de normativas legales y éticas en la obtención de información', and decisions it called 'evidentemente precipitadas y temerarias'; it also criticised BCCR general manager Hazel Valverde for filing a criminal complaint against SUGEF head Rocío Aguilar before the Procuraduría General had given its opinion. The six votes in favour were Dinorah Barquero, Francisco Nicolás and Carolina Delgado (PLN), Vanessa Castro (PUSC), Kattia Cambronero (PLP) and Fabricio Alvarado (Nueva República); the three against were Sofía Guillén (FA) and Ada Acuña and Daniel Vargas. The date is the article's publication date of 18 April 2024, which reports the approval as having happened that day; no separate approval date is printed. This is a different organ and a different proceeding from the two Costa Rican records already on the map: the January 2024 ministerial demand on exchange-rate policy (event index 194) and the criminal case against SUGEF's Rocío Aguilar arising from the same data dispute (case index 238), in which Madrigal is a witness rather than the subject.
records.source_title: Comisión legislativa aprueba informe que recomienda destituir a Róger Madrigal — CRHoy, 18 April 2024

records.summary: A formal written objection to a draft federal law was lodged in the Austrian Nationalrat's consultation procedure on 6 May 2014 by the Zentralbetriebsrat of the Oesterreichische Nationalbank, the central bank's own central works council, against the draft Sonderpensionenbegrenzungsgesetz (SpBegrG), which would have extended the constitutional cap on public functionaries' remuneration and the 2012 Stability Act's pension contributions to OeNB staff and pensioners. Filed as 241/SN-16/ME XXV. GP on the parliament's own site, the submission argues that enacting the bill would have the legislature intervene directly in the business competence of the OeNB's Generalrat, which under section 21(1) of the Nationalbankgesetz is the organ responsible for staff regulations and for the rules governing those persons' pay and pensions: 'Mit Beschlussfassung des Gesetzes wie vorliegend würde der Gesetzgeber direkt in die Geschäftsbefugnis des Generalrates als zuständiges Organ eingreifen.' It states that the interference in central bank affairs the draft provides for is incompatible with the EU-law principle of central bank autonomy and independence and, in the works council's legal view, breaches Article 130 TFEU, and that the statutory obligation to levy pension contributions in order to raise state revenue is to be seen as a breach of Article 123 TFEU. The objection is the works council's, acting for serving and retired staff, and not a resolution of the bank's governing organs, and the subject matter is staff pensions rather than monetary policy; both qualifications are stated here because the submission itself states them. The source is a submission on a draft, not a statute, so no in-force check applies to it. Distinct from the April 2019 record already on the map.
records.source_title: 241/SN-16/ME XXV. GP — Stellungnahme des Zentralbetriebsrates der Oesterreichischen Nationalbank zum Entwurf eines Sonderpensionenbegrenzungsgesetzes, 6 May 2014, Parlament Österreich
records.quote: Nach der Rechtsmeinung des ZBR verstößt die unzulässige Einmischung des Staates gegen Art. 130 AEUV.

records.summary: After the Junta Directiva of the Banco de la República raised its policy interest rate, President Gustavo Petro attacked the board publicly on X, saying that what the board's majority had done was an electoral rather than a scientific act — 'Lo que hizo la mayoría de la junta del Banco de la República es un acto electoral y no científico' — and that the board is not independent. He said the decision served to fill the pockets of holders of national public debt securities, and faulted the bank for not coordinating the decision with the Government, which he said the 1991 Constitution requires. The date is the Colprensa report's publication date of 4 April 2026. This is a separate statement on a separate rate decision from the July 2025 episode already on the map (index 37), in which Petro accused the bank of having an electoral bet; the two are the same head of state and the same complaint but different dates and different monetary decisions, and a curator may prefer to treat them as one running episode.
records.source_title: Petro arremete nuevamente contra el Banco de la República y cuestiona su independencia — Vanguardia / Colprensa, 4 April 2026

blanks.read: A real candidate refused on the date rule and on shape. Montenegro Business, 'Setback in Central Bank leadership appointments challenges institutional independence in Montenegro', published 21 May 2025 (https://montenegrobusiness.eu/setback-in-central-bank-leadership-appointments-challenges-institutional-independence-in-montenegro/), read in full: the Parliament of Montenegro did not give the required support to the two nominees for vice-governor of the Central Bank of Montenegro, Gordana Kaležić and Milan Remiković, nominated in August 2024 and, the article says, unobjected to since; the CBCG's Communications Directorate is reported as calling the failure a setback for the bank's full functionality and institutional independence and as citing the Central Bank Law and EU principles of central bank independence. Refused for two reasons. First, the article gives no date for the vote at all — only 'the recent vote' — so any date I wrote would be the publication date standing in for the event, which this round's rule forbids. Second, a parliament declining to confirm nominees is an omission rather than the state removing, suspending, prosecuting, investigating or legislating against the bank, and the row has refused adjacent shapes before. One fetch of the Skupština's own voting record for the relevant sitting would fix the date and make this filable; that is the named next step. Also surfaced and not opened: novosti.rs on President Milatovic withdrawing his own proposal of Radoje Žugić for a third term as governor, which is a withdrawal of the state's own nomination rather than an act against the bank.

A real candidate refused because the source reports an intention and not an act. Noviny.sk, 'Politico: Tvrdá politická bitka o guvernéra Národnej banky Slovenska', published 14 August 2025 (https://www.noviny.sk/slovensko/1095587-politico-tvrda-politicka-bitka-o-guvernera-narodnej-banky-slovenska), read in full: citing Politico and unnamed sources, it reports that Prime Minister Robert Fico wants to remove the over-serving governor Peter Kažimír and replace him with Finance Minister Ladislav Kamenický ('Premiér Robert Fico chce odvolatí už nadsluhujúceho Petra Kažimíra'); Kamenický called the report speculation and said 'že nič také nie je na stole'; President Pellegrini and HLAS are reported as backing Kažimír; the NBS and Kažimír did not comment. The article states expressly that the government had not proposed a new governor and reports no formal step and no legislation. An anonymously sourced reported intention, publicly denied by the minister named in it, is not an organ of the state acting on the bank. Separately refused by the row's own rule: Kažimír's bribery conviction and the 200,000-euro fine are a prosecution of an individual for his own conduct as finance minister, and that episode is already on the corruption row for Slovakia (case index 89). Also checked and not applicable: the ECB's own Governing Council decisions page for November 2025 (https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/govcdec/otherdec/2025/html/ecb.gc251121~4807dec7cf.sk.html) lists Opinions CON/2025/33 to CON/2025/37 and the only national ones are Slovenian and Italian, not Slovak; the Slovak-language press hits for ECB opinions concern the bank levy and a financial transaction tax, which fall on commercial banks and not on the NBS. The ECB-opinion vein named in the round-73 brief therefore produced nothing for Slovakia this round, and lagen.nu remains robots-disallowed.

Searched for a second Moroccan episode and found only the same family already on the map. A French-language search for a parliamentary inquiry commission, a summons of Wali Abdellatif Jouahri or a legislative move against Bank Al-Maghrib returned: Medias24's 2020 pieces on the parliamentary mission on the banking sector and on Jouahri's 24 November 2020 hearing before the Chambre des représentants' finance committee; Le360's 'Taux directeur: Jouahri, Fettah et Lahlimi dans l'œil du cyclone', which is the same policy-rate criticism family as the March 2023 record already on the map (index 168); Hespress on Jouahri announcing meetings with the GPBM and the finance committee, on Bank Al-Maghrib asking that the digital-currency bill be prioritised, and on Jouahri's retrospective of 23 years as governor; and Bladi on Jouahri urging an investigation into the Bab Darna property scam, which is the bank as detector. A routine appearance of a governor before a standing finance committee is not a move against the bank, and nothing returned shows a removal, suspension, prosecution, inquiry or bill aimed at Bank Al-Maghrib. No Moroccan document was downloaded. Named next step: the Chambre des représentants' own site (representantsd10.fornetmaroc.com surfaced a finance and economic development committee page naming Bank Al-Maghrib) and the Chambre's published committee minutes, which were not opened for want of budget.

No Guatemalan document opened. A Spanish search for a congressional move against Banco de Guatemala — a reform of its Ley Orgánica, an interpellation of the Junta Monetaria — returned only the bank's own publications: the 'Proyecto de Ley Orgánica del Banco de Guatemala' page and bgcom002.pdf on banguat.gob.gt, the bank's own Informe al Congreso for January 2023, its Memorias de Labores for 2023 and 2024, its organisational descriptions and budget files, and a vLex copy of Decreto 16-2002. None of these is a state organ acting against the bank; they are the bank reporting to Congress, which is the opposite direction. Guatemala's one record is the 2016 prosecution of Banguat president Julio Suárez (index 158), which is also on the corruption row as index 111 with an acquitted outcome. Named next steps, neither opened: the Congreso de la República's own iniciativas de ley register for any bill amending Decreto 16-2002, and the Corte de Constitucionalidad's published judgments for any challenge to the Junta Monetaria's composition.

Searched and the only thing found was the record already on the map, which is the finding this round most wants written down. A search for an Uzbek dismissal, senate removal or presidential decree against the Central Bank returned kun.uz on President Mirziyoyev proposing the Central Bank chairman's resignation on 11 December 2024 — which is index 163, already filed from that exact kun.uz story — plus qalampir.uz and daryo.uz on the Senate approving the dismissal of Mamarizo Nurmuratov on the same day, which is the same episode at its next procedural step, spot.uz on his 2022 reappointment, fergana.agency and buzb.uz on Timur Ishmetov's appointment as successor, and intellinews on the death of the long-serving earlier chief Faizulla Mullajanov. Nothing returned concerns a second, earlier Uzbek removal with a stated cause, and an unexplained replacement would fail this row's settled doctrine in any case. Named next step if reopened: the Senate's own stenographic record of the 11 December 2024 sitting, which would give the grounds the press paraphrased, and the Oliy Majlis site for any amendment to the Law on the Central Bank.

No Lesotho document opened. A search for a suspension, dismissal, ministerial board inquiry or governor dispute at the Central Bank of Lesotho returned the bank's own press statement 'End of Term of Office of the Governor and Deputy Governors', 4 January 2022 (https://centralbank.org.ls/wp-content/uploads/Press_Statement_Governors_End_of_Term_040122_Eng.pdf), which is an ordinary expiry of term and not a removal; thereporter.co.ls on the new governor; allAfrica on a Revenue Services Lesotho board dispute involving Matlanyane in her later ministerial capacity, which is not the central bank; centralbanking on Lesotho appointing a governance trio and on a former governor becoming finance minister, both of which are career moves and belong on the other row; and the Wikipedia article on the bank. The one record the map holds for Lesotho on this row is the June 2026 Public Accounts Committee call for a forensic audit into the missing M3.9 billion (index 167). Named next steps, neither opened and both carried over from round 72's case-row notes: the Office of the Auditor General Lesotho's own report index, and the National Assembly's published PAC minutes rather than the press reports of them.

The Algerian document exists and the host is still unreachable, for the fourth round running on any row. The route identified is the Banque d'Algérie's own 'Point de situation sur le financement non conventionnel' page and its 'intervention_apn122018fr.pdf', the Governor's December 2018 address to the Assemblée Populaire Nationale, both of which a search returned on the bank's own host: www.bank-of-algeria.dz returned HTTP 000 with zero bytes to curl on both paths, and WebFetch refused the page as robots_disallowed. Those documents would show on the bank's own words whether the 2017 amendment to the Loi sur la monnaie et le credit obliging the Treasury to be financed directly by the Bank was imposed on it, which is the family this row files. Also surfaced and not opened, all on reachable hosts: tsa-algerie.com, 'Planche a billets: la Banque d'Algérie règle ses comptes avec Ouyahia et Bouteflika', which on its title alone appears to be the bank criticising the government that imposed the arrangement; le360's 'Algérie: neuf ans après, la planche à billets n'a jamais été débranchée'; and a Mila university journal article on the law. The single record Algeria holds on this row is the May 2022 dismissal of the governor by President Tebboune (index 161). Named next step: fetch the tsa-algerie piece, which is on a host that serves, and use it to date and characterise the 2017 statutory obligation; then check whether Ordinance 03-11's article 45 bis survives the 2023 monetary and banking law before filing the statute itself.

No Salvadoran document opened. A Spanish search for a legislative investigative commission or a law obliging the Banco Central de Reserva returned only digital-asset material: Diario El Mundo on the government asking for anti-money-laundering rules to be reformed for bitcoin services and on the Assembly amending the Ley de Activos Digitales so the bitcoin agency can receive state funds, Observador on El Salvador withdrawing bitcoin's legal-tender status, criptonoticias on the investment-banking law, and four jurisprudencia.gob.sv decree and judgment PDFs including Decreto No. 199, none of which was opened and none of which a search snippet shows to be about the central bank as subject. The Bitcoin Law family is the most promising untested vein here — a statute that assigned the BCR duties over a currency it does not issue — but it needs the decree text read, not a press summary. El Salvador's one record is the September 2020 parliamentary inquiry (index 214). Named next step: jurisprudencia.gob.sv for Decreto Legislativo 57 of 2021 and for Decreto No. 199, read for what they require of the Banco Central de Reserva and whether the bank is recorded as having objected.

The vein is real and the index that would open it does not list titles. The Vanuatu Ombudsman's public reports are the source of the single record Vanuatu holds on this row (paclii.org/vu/other/ombudsman/1996/12.html, the 1996 report on Governor Samson Ngwele, filed on both rows), and the database holds 163 reports from 1996 to 2020. The database landing page at https://pacliirms.austlii.edu.au/vu/other/ombudsman was fetched and read: it gives the collection's size, the span of years and the browse options, and displays no report titles at all, so the inversion test cannot be run from it and no second Reserve Bank of Vanuatu report could be identified without opening year pages one at a time. Search returned fifteen individual report URLs (1996/8 to 1996/11, 1997/4, 1999/1, 1999/12, 2001/7, 2003/10, 2005/5, 2011/2, 2012/1, 2016/3, 2017/1) with no titles, so opening them would be blind. Named next step, cheap for a round with budget: fetch the year-index pages paclii.org/vu/other/ombudsman/1997 through /2005, which do carry report titles, and look for the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu as subject.

Searched in Portuguese for a second Angolan removal and found none with a stated cause. The search returned lex.ao's presidential-decree series (Decretos Presidenciais 139/23 and 135/23 of June 2023, 260/17 and 264/17 and 267/17 of late 2017, and several 2015 and 2016 decrees), verangola on five new ministers and a new BNA governor being named in December 2016, verangola's own October 2017 piece which is the exact source already filed as index 164, forbesafricalusofona on João Lourenço exonerating the BNA governor and appointing him Minister of State for Economic Coordination, and rr.pt and eco.sapo.pt on the volume of Lourenço's dismissals in his first year. The Massano move to Minister of State is a promotion into government, not a removal under pressure, and belongs on the career row rather than this one; the December 2016 replacement of a governor is an unexplained substitution, which this row's settled doctrine refuses. No Angolan document was downloaded. Named next step: lex.ao's decree texts themselves, since an Angolan presidential decree of exoneration sometimes recites a ground, which the press reports do not.

blanks.country: ARE, BEN, BHS, BRB, CAF, CMR, CYM, ERI, GAB, GNB, HTI, JAM, KHM, PSE, SEN, TJK
blanks.read: Sixteen of the thirty-four assigned places were not tested at all, and this is a budget note rather than a finding, so that the next round does not read them as searched. Every one of them had its have_events.json and have_cases.json entry read, and searched.json shows none of them has ever been worked on this row. The grounds for skipping each: ARE, BHS, CYM, ERI, KHM, PSE and TJK already hold a statutory-arrangement record, so a second record there means a different provision of the same statute or a distinct episode, and the statute route needs an in-force check that costs a fetch each. BEN, GNB and SEN hold the same BCEAO record expanded into three members (the January 2011 forced resignation of Governor Dacoury-Tabley), and CAF, CMR and GAB the same BEAC record, so for those six a national finding would be the country's first own record on this row; round 72 proved on the case row that the national institutions of BCEAO and BEAC members cannot reach the union, and the right route is a national finance ministry or national assembly acting on the union's national directorate, which was not attempted. BRB's single record is the 2017 dismissal of Governor DeLisle Worrell, and the injunction and appeal litigation around it is the same episode, not a second one. JAM's route is japarliament.gov.jm, which is where the existing record came from, and HTI's is the Cour Supérieure des Comptes et du Contentieux Administratif budget-execution and RSFPEDP series, both named in earlier rounds' case-row notes and both multi-megabyte downloads. Nothing here is a documented blank.

checked_not_in_assignment.note: Surfaced by the ECB Governing Council decisions page for November 2025 as the subject of Opinion CON/2025/33, on the independence of Banka Slovenije's Governing Council members and the prevention of conflicts of interest. Looked up before pursuing: have_events.json holds two counted events for Slovenia (a 2016-07-06 seizure and a 2019-10-16 attempted law change), so it is not an exactly-one place and is not a target. searched.json records Slovenia only under reserve_managers and one unknown row. Not pursued.

Surfaced by the same ECB page as the subject of Opinion CON/2025/36, on the independence of Banca d'Italia in supervision and the exercise of administrative discretion over mergers and qualifying holdings. Looked up before pursuing: have_events.json holds two counted events for Italy (2005-12-19 resignation under pressure and 2017-10-17 public pressure), so it is not an exactly-one place. searched.json records Italy only under reserve_managers. Not pursued. Worth flagging for whoever builds the next targets list: CON/2025/36 is a live ECB opinion on a draft Italian law touching the bank's supervisory independence, and the ECB-opinion vein the round-73 brief named is still unworked on these two countries.

leads_not_opened.lead: The National Audit Office of Tanzania publishes a report per sector per year on nao.go.tz at predictable paths, and the Bank of Tanzania is an audited entity in the Public Authorities and Other Bodies series. The 2007/2008 report alone carries at least five separate BoT matters beyond the one filed: a motor-vehicle finding at section 9.2.3, 'Bank of Tanzania's vehicles Registered in Private' names; 'BoT Lacks integrated policies on Money Laundering'; 'Weaknesses in Management of BOT Loans for Refinancing'; a finding on the contract for the BoT Head Office Extension Project with a named counterparty; and a board-composition note. The later reports in the same series (Public Authorities and Other Bodies 2012/13 and the Central Government reports) are on the same host and open to plain curl at about 700 kB each. This is the annual-series vein the depth brief describes, and Tanzania is the clearest example of it found this round.

The Bank of Mauritius's own site serves documents to WebFetch but refused curl with a TLS failure. Two named documents not read: 'public_notice_clarification_transfer_of_rs60_billion_0.pdf' and 'public_notice_-_treatment_of_one-off_exceptional_contribution_of_rs60_billion_to_government_-_7_may_2021.pdf', both on bom.mu, which are the Bank's own account of the Rs 60 billion transfer to Government made under the COVID-19 (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2020 amendments to the Bank of Mauritius Act. If those notices record the Bank as having been obliged to make the transfer, that is this row's 'law obliging the bank to do something it objected to'; if they record the Bank as having agreed to it, the row refuses it, and that distinction is exactly what the documents would settle. The statute text itself is hard to reach: covidlawlab.org's ACT012023 path served HTML under a .pdf name (344,234 bytes that pdftotext rejected) and MRA.mu returned HTTP 000.

The Austrian parliament's Stellungnahme archive on parlament.gv.at serves PDFs to plain curl at two path shapes (/PAKT/VHG/<GP>/SNME/SNME_<nnnnn>/imfname_<n>.pdf and /dokument/<GP>/SNME/<n>/imfname_<n>.pdf) and is a primary record of who objected to which bill and why. One fetch spent on XXVIII/SNME/550 returned a Bundeskanzleramt submission on an information-freedom bill, not an OeNB one, so the archive needs to be searched by the bank's name rather than by legislative period. Untested and named: whether the Oesterreichische Nationalbank itself, as distinct from its works council, has filed a Stellungnahme on any draft law, and the ECB opinion CON/2001/10, which a search surfaced for Austria on the robots-disallowed lagen.nu mirror and which the depth brief says can sometimes be reached through ecb.europa.eu/ecb/legal/pdf/ paths.

Not opened for want of budget, and all on hosts that serve: L'Orient Today's 'How the Lebanese investigation targeting Riad Salameh is being systematically impeded' and 'At BDL, Ghada Aoun returns to the fray in vain', and The National's 19 July 2022 report of the raid, whose URL carries the day and would settle the exact date this record leaves at month precision. The National's piece also states security personnel raided the bank, where Al Jazeera says only 'judicial raid'.

Two Costa Rican documents named and not opened, both of which would upgrade the filed record from press to primary: delfino.cr's record of Asamblea Legislativa motion 202502172, and the Observador pieces on the creation of the comisión investigadora over the Banco Central's request for individualised data and on the deputies drafting its final recommendations. The Asamblea Legislativa publishes its commission reports in full, and the report recommending Madrigal's dismissal should be retrievable by its expediente number.
